research_question: Can the already-frozen one-sided-inequality-plus-parity formulation produce a noncircular same-E/Q comparison between the independently defined Kurihara discrete order and the complex Taylor order, without assuming BSD/analytic-rank equality?

primary_sources.title: On the Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer quotients modulo squares
primary_sources.verified_claim: For every elliptic curve E/Q and every prime p, the p-parity conjecture holds: the parity of the p-infinity Selmer rank agrees with the analytic rank/root-number parity.
primary_sources.scope_note: This is a Selmer-parity theorem; no Mordell-Weil rank equality or Sha finiteness is inserted.

primary_sources.author: Chan-Ho Kim
primary_sources.title: The structure of Selmer groups and the Iwasawa main conjecture for elliptic curves
primary_sources.version_note: arXiv v6 last revised 2025-05-14; current manuscript text displays date 2026-03-21
verified_claims: Under the theorem's p>=5, residual-surjectivity, Manin-constant and finite-Kurihara-order hypotheses, the classical p-infinity Selmer structure is determined by the Kurihara collection; in particular its Z_p-corank equals the discrete Kurihara order.
For good ordinary p under the stated residual hypotheses, the relevant Iwasawa-main-conjecture input is available and the Kurihara collection is nonzero, so the structural theorem applies.
The paper derives p-parity and a computational upper bound, while presenting the discrete variation as a BSD-type analogue rather than an arbitrary-rank identity with the complex Taylor order.
strict_nonclaims: The audited theorem does not identify the Kurihara order with ord_{s=1}L(E,s) in arbitrary rank.
It does not provide the refined complex BSD leading-term identity.

primary_sources.title: The refined Tamagawa number conjectures for GL_2
verified_claims: Under large-image and localized-Iwasawa hypotheses, exact Bloch-Kato Selmer rank/module structure is recovered from Kolyvagin derivatives of special L-values.
The formula is explicitly designed to be insensitive to analytic rank and uses a discrete derivative rather than complex or p-adic Taylor variation.
The source supplies Kurihara/Kolyvagin nonvanishing routes in low-rank or localized-main-conjecture/good-ordinary cells, not an arbitrary-rank complex Taylor-order equality.
primary_sources.route_role: 2026 frontier cross-check that stronger discrete arithmetic reconstruction still leaves the complex/discrete magnitude comparison open

exact_composition.statement: In any E/Q,p theorem cell in which Kim's exact classical p-infinity Selmer structure theorem gives ord_Kur(E,p)=corank_Zp Sel(Q,E[p^infinity]), Dokchitser-Dokchitser p-parity composes to ord_Kur(E,p) congruent to ord_{s=1}L(E,s) modulo 2.
proof_steps: Kim gives exact equality between the independently defined discrete Kurihara order and the corank of the classical p-infinity Selmer group under explicit hypotheses.
Dokchitser-Dokchitser gives equality modulo 2 between that p-infinity Selmer rank and the complex analytic rank for every E/Q and p.
Both edges use the same curve and classical p-primary Selmer coordinate, so transitivity modulo 2 yields the scoped complex/discrete parity relation.
exact_composition.scope: source-bound composition only; no literature-novelty claim

rank_two_corollary.statement: Where the canonical R9 Zhang technical-prime cell and the R14 Kim parity cell overlap, exact analytic rank two implies ord_Kur(E,p) is an even integer at least 2, hence belongs to {2,4,6,...}.
rank_two_corollary.reason: R9 gives p-infinity Selmer corank >=2; Kim identifies that corank with the Kurihara order in its cell; R14 parity makes the order even.
rank_two_corollary.strict_nonclaim: No upper bound excludes 4,6,..., so this does not prove exact Kurihara order two or BSD rank two.

counterexample_first_falsifier.meaning: Parity cannot force equality of integer orders; a root-relevant closure still requires a same-coordinate magnitude inequality/equality strong enough to exclude discrepancy 2 or more.
